reason: E1 describes crack propagation along lamellar interfaces due to stress accumulation, supporting the problem of pile-up, but does not show that refining spacing solves it. E2 demonstrates a nano-lamellar structure with high strength and some ductility in a different HEA system, but it is achieved by a solid-state eutectoid reaction, not by cold-rolling and annealing of a eutectic HEA. The specific processing route, its effect on interlamellar spacing in eutectic HEAs, and the claimed back-stress hardening mechanism are not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Refining lamellar spacing reduces dislocation pile-up length and local stress concentrations
Cold-rolling + low-temperature annealing can refine interlamellar spacing from micron to sub-micron/nanometer scale in eutectic HEAs
Finer lamellar architecture increases phase boundary density, enabling strain partitioning and back-stress hardening
Back-stress hardening from refined lamellae can maintain or increase strength while improving ductility
The proposed processing avoids undesirable phase transformations and excessive refinement that would cause brittleness
